digest.component_or_area: transition-request value object and close-reason/force rule consolidation
propositions: Close-reason and force plumbing logic is duplicated across three surfaces: CLI (transition.py:584), library (_lib_writes.py:318), and MCP (_mcp_writes.py:224-232), with the rule 'reason persists only on REASON_REQUIRED class without force' computed independently in each.

The CLI refuses inadmissible reasons (exit 1) while the library silently discards them (returns 0), and MCP transition_ticket does not expose reason at all; no merge of the three implementations leaves all pinning tests green.

The '(no reason given)' placeholder literal appears in five code sites across three files but must be produced in exactly one place as a named constant with a guard assertion; docstrings and comments that name the placeholder are legitimately out of scope.

A bare --force close of a reason-required class must remain accepted; the normalization of empty reason to placeholder must occur before the refusal check at txn.py:232 to avoid flipping acceptance to refusal.
The placeholder must never reach close_disposition.verdict, which fails closed on empty reason and would turn an UNJUSTIFIED disposition into a SIGNED one if given the normalized placeholder.

The library's _lib_writes.transition(force_close=) is a deprecated public alias while close_ticket(force_close=) is an internal parameter name; a convergence must not conflate the two distinct semantics or break pinned source-text inspection in three existing tests.
